The verdict is **fix**: three things need changing, plus four smaller observations. The review covers step 1 only (the phase-0 fixes), because that is all the diff contains. I wrote it to `chat-model/review.md`. This diff changes no page, so the review has only the Requirements and Words sections and no screenshots.

**Must change:**
1. **Fix 2 now makes duplicate lines in one case.** A tab's post now carries its own id (`client`), but the copy it appends as a fallback when the post is slow does not. So when the post finally lands after the fallback has already written the line, the duplicate check misses it and the line is written twice. `doc/one-writer.md:231` says this can't happen. The existing test for this order (`one-writer.test.mjs:103`) still passes only because it posts without a `client`, which no real tab does any more.
2. **Fix 1 is marked "Done" but covers one write path out of three.** The newline guard is only in `RecordWriter.append_once`. The two paths most writes go through still append without it: `write_line` in `page_tools.js` (Servex's entry point) and the dev server's `Append.js`.
3. **Fix 5 changes how a new list item is saved, and some readers weren't checked.** Its fields are now saved under `data` instead of at the top level. `rail.js:484`, `Activity.js:143` and `SessionTimelineRows.js:97` read those fields from the top level, so a card added from the browser would show up blank in those summaries.

**Worth a look:**
- `SessionConsolidate.mjs` still rewrites files the unsafe way; the new safe-write helper is used by only one caller.
- The temporary file the helper writes during each save sends a live-reload notice to every tab. Probably harmless, but not checked.
- Fix 3 has no test, and status.md doesn't link to the code that proves it.
- Steps 2–8 aren't built yet, and child task `s1` is still open.

**Tests:** everything that exists passes. The test runner gives 22 of 22 over `core/Item` and `core/List`, and the five new or changed test files pass when run directly.

I've reviewed step 3 of the chat model (tasks and child sessions as Refs in the chat list), and the verdict is **fix**. The 17 checks in `chat-messages.test.mjs` all pass in the worktree. The report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/chat-model/review/report.md`.

## What needs fixing
- **Nested sessions get no Ref for their child sessions.** `SessionRecord.is_chat_ref_target` only accepts a session folder that sits directly under a day. A session one level deeper, like `chat-model` itself, fails that test. So its own minion spawn (line 66 of its `session.jsonl`) would get no Ref, while a task added to the same file does get one. The plan's decision 3 says Refs go on every session record.
- **The readme claims more than the code does.** Line 56 of `core/Session/Chat/readme.md` says every spawned child session gets a Ref and doesn't mention the nested-session gap.
- **The merge would mark live files as deleted.** `ai/sessions/files.jsonl` gains 11 "gone" lines (`transcripts/`, `week.json`, `index.jsonl` and others). Those files are gitignored and still exist in the main tree; the worktree simply doesn't have them.

## Smaller notes
- Only the inline-subtask Ref and `add_ref` are tested. Adding a task that makes its own folder has no test.
- Every Ref is stamped `by: "servex"`, even when another script wrote it.
- The screenshots are of the builder page, which this diff doesn't change. At 1920 the page's task section has zero height, so the page is 88% empty. That bug was there before this change and needs its own task.
- The new readme paragraph runs about 150 words, and the file names in it aren't linked.

**Must change:**
1. **The "V1 way" isn't what V1 draws.** `Chat.js` `place()` moves each new bubble into time order, but `V1Bubbles.bubbles()` keeps the lines in file order. So the doc's explanation for why so many bubbles differ (1114 of 1247 in one session, 591 of 729 in another) isn't proven. The compare should be re-run once the mirror also orders by time.
2. **The doc contradicts `s8/compare.txt`.** It says `v-timqv56` was the one session that didn't need `plan()`, but compare.txt shows it did. The real exception is `v-u48msei`, and that session is only partly mirrored.
3. **The first gate can't be measured.** `ChatV1Compare.mjs` treats any file with even one `messages` line as fully mirrored. So `v-u48msei` (278 bubbles from V1 against 63 from the adapter) would already pass "0 sessions still needing `plan()`".
4. **The new test and tool aren't indexed.** The readme's "Check it" section lists neither `V1Bubbles.test.mjs` nor `ChatV1Compare.mjs`.

**Notes:**
- The compare script writes a temp file and reads it straight back for no reason.
- The real-fixture check in the test is true by construction, so it can't catch a merge bug.
- The adapter skips `fix` lines but keeps the old text, while V1 shows the corrected text. Those lines will show up as false text differences.
- `Server/doc/scripts.md` has no row for the new script.

Review fixes are landed and logged. Here's the final status:

### Step 8: V1 side by side — review fixes landed (fc109ec8e)

**Fixed per the mastermind's 7 points:**
1. `V1Bubbles.bubbles()` now mirrors `place()`'s time-reordering and `fix`/revision in-place resolution (not just append+skip)
2. Mirror coverage is now `full`/`partial`/`none` (measured from actual `{chat}`-line-to-mirror matching), not a presence check
3. The adapter reads `Prompt.clean` so a `{place}` improve shows the same corrected text V1 shows
4. Dropped the temp-file write/read round trip — `ChatToMessages.plan()` called directly, still never `--apply`'d
5. `doc/pseudo-properties.md` rewritten with the real numbers and the real cause
6. `V1Bubbles.test.mjs` + `ChatV1Compare.mjs` indexed in readme.md's "Check it" and `Server/doc/scripts.md`
7. Replaced the true-by-construction test with one that exercises merge + `place()` reordering + `fix` together (and would have caught the original bug)

**Real finding (not the reply-hold theory — that was wrong):** `said_at` is never mirrored onto a Sentence or Message at all (grep-confirmed). V1 orders/merges by `said_at ?? at`; the adapter can only read `at`. That's the entire explanation for the two big sessions' cascading diffs.

**New per-session counts** (`compare.txt` in the main tree):
| session | mirror | V1 | adapter | differing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v-sq8y7db | none | 1314 | 1215 | 1183 |
| v-9dvbbrn | none | 765 | 703 | 716 |
| v-u48msei | **partial** | 278 | 63 | 278 |
| v-yxnts4l | none | 215 | 216 | 7 |
| v-timqv56 | none | 170 | 170 | **0** |

The two `said_at`-free sessions (`v-yxnts4l`, `v-timqv56`) confirm the theory: 7 and 0 diffs vs. hundreds on the two sessions carrying `said_at`.

**Tests:** `V1Bubbles.test.mjs` 6/6 checks; full `core/Session` suite 5/5 pass.

I re-reviewed step 8 (the side-by-side check of V1 against `session.messages`), and my verdict is **fix**. The report is at `chat-model/review.md`.

All 8 findings from the earlier step-8 review are fixed. `V1Bubbles.test.mjs` passes its 6 checks in the worktree.

**What must change before the merge:**
1. **The migration plan can't run as written.** The switch-over doc (`pseudo-properties.md:41,45`) says to migrate partly mirrored sessions with `ChatToMessages.mjs --apply`, including `v-u48msei`. But `ChatToMessages.mjs:24` skips any file that already has a `messages` or `sentences` line, so those sessions can never be migrated. Either let it fill in only the missing lines, or say in the doc that partial sessions have no migration path yet.
2. **Wrong index lines again.** Commit `d17eeb380` ("worktree housekeeping (index churn)") marks about 25 entries in `files.jsonl` index files as deleted. I checked, and every one of those files still exists in the main tree. It's the same worktree indexer bug the step-3 review found, so that commit should be dropped and the bug filed as its own task.

**Notes, not blocking:**
- **The builder's diagnosis is right.** I re-ran the compare with the `said_at` timestamps removed. The differences dropped from 1183 to 2 on `v-sq8y7db` and from 716 to 0 on `v-9dvbbrn`. That's stronger proof than the doc currently gives, and it's worth adding there.
- **One small mismatch with V1.** When a correction arrives for a line that isn't on screen, V1 draws it as its own line, but the mirror throws it away (`V1Bubbles.js:65`).
- **The test on the real session proves little.** It can't fail, because each sentence is counted exactly once by design. The new made-up test does cover merging, reordering and corrections.
- **One self-contradicting line in the doc.** It says "Nothing here is built yet" while step 1 is marked done.
